headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk: Haystack can ingest MCP/API content while LlamaFactory is a non-networked local agent, creating a one-way trust boundary with limited leakage but real misinterpretation risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack exposes REST APIs and MCP servers with broad network egress, so it can ingest attacker-controlled content. LlamaFactory has no MCP, clipboard, or filesystem bridge, so the pair lacks a direct shared channel by default; however, Haystack’s permissive ingestion surface makes prompt injection plausible if its outputs are later consumed as instructions.
conditions: IF Haystack ingests untrusted MCP or REST payloads as instructions, injection is possible.
IF LlamaFactory is manually fed Haystack output as prompt text, the attack path opens.
mitigations: Restrict Haystack MCP endpoints to trusted clients only.
Add provenance labels to all Haystack outputs.
Disable copy-paste of raw model output into LlamaFactory prompts.
Use a fixed instruction template that separates data from directives.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing for Haystack inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack touches anonymous usage statistics and has broad network egress, but LlamaFactory has no filesystem read, no network egress, and no data classes touched. There is no shared workspace or authenticated principal shown, so leakage between the pair is limited and not default-dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents are placed on the same shared workspace, leakage risk increases.
IF Haystack is configured to forward retrieved content into external services, data exposure expands.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any optional Haystack telemetry beyond anonymous stats.
Review outbound destinations for Haystack.
Avoid passing sensitive documents through Haystack.
requires-engineering: enforce OS-level sandboxing between the two agents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and MCP/API access, but LlamaFactory cannot write files, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, or use MCP. With no overlapping write surface or shared mutable resource in the profiles, a capability conflict pathway is not evident.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory is wrapped by an external orchestrator that grants write access, conflict could emerge.
IF both agents are later given the same mutable resource, reassess.
mitigations: Keep LlamaFactory read-only.
Do not grant shared git or filesystem write access.
Separate network credentials per agent.
Document resource ownership before deployment.
requires-engineering: add locking for any future shared mutable store.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack can produce retrieved facts or generated answers, and LlamaFactory is a customer-support agent that may consume those outputs. Because LlamaFactory has no built-in verification surface shown, Haystack’s output can become authoritative by workflow, creating a plausible cascade even though the exact integration is undocumented.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory uses Haystack output as a source of truth, errors can cascade.
IF a human review step is inserted before actioning, the risk drops.
mitigations: Require human review of Haystack-derived answers.
Tag Haystack output as unverified in downstream prompts.
Add a verification checklist before customer replies.
Limit LlamaFactory to drafting, not sending, responses.
requires-engineering: implement citation and confidence checks.

E_compliance.rationale: Haystack is documented as touching anonymous usage statistics, while LlamaFactory lists no data classes touched and no special residency or retention obligations. The profiles do not show a concrete compliance mismatch, so only a small residual risk remains from unspecified logging or telemetry differences.
conditions: IF Haystack is configured to process regulated data, compliance review is needed.
IF LlamaFactory is deployed with a stricter retention policy than Haystack, mismatch risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in Haystack.
Confirm retention settings for Haystack telemetry.
Keep LlamaFactory outputs free of personal data.
Record data-flow ownership for both agents.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion controls.
